correctness.rationale: The frozen Finding's unqualified independence away from the degenerate axis is false if taken pointwise. For example at the upper pole with R>0 the restriction of dH to the cylinder is zero, so dH is proportional to dP. In fact at that equilibrium the full linearization has rank two; differentiating X(I)=0 there shows that any smooth first integral has differential in its one-dimensional left kernel. The delivered replacement states and proves the exact independence locus for the displayed pair: on R>0, dP is nonzero, the global periodic angular primitive is smooth, and dH restricted to the cylinder is gk y dy−F_R(θ)dθ, which vanishes exactly at cylinder equilibria. The repaired text also specifies that the cross-section is circular in scaled coordinates. Rechecking the surviving result: the angular equation yields the indicated pole derivatives and the Hamiltonian gives nonlinear center behavior when F_R'<0. Locally z<0 and sinc(x)>0, so equating z=−b sinc(x) and squaring preserves equivalence to the scalar equation. In t=x² its quadratic coefficient is h=2kb²/45 and G_tt>h on a fixed small t-interval. A sufficiently small joint parameter box keeps G above ε at the outer endpoint; convexity gives all stated counts. At δ=0 inversion gives the fourth-root pair only for ε>0, with the stated error. At δ<0 the implicit-function theorem gives t_f=−δ/(2h)+O(δ²)>0 and its height −δ²/(4h)+O(|δ|³). The fold is nondegenerate in the scalar equation and occurs at both signs of x. Rationalizing the local force verifies that at each root F_R' has the sign of G_t, so the inner pair is elliptic and the outer pair hyperbolic on the cylinder. The base point itself is nonhyperbolic; no full-space stability inference is made.
residual_risks: Independence is not asserted at equilibria. Local equilibrium counts and relative stability do not supply global counts or persistence off the conservative boundary. The finite companion diagnostics do not prove the analytic assertions.

value.rationale: The conservative unforced limit is a natural boundary of an independently studied sine flow, not a parameter slice chosen merely to fit a predetermined expansion. On that boundary an explicit invariant-cylinder diagram answers where the ordinary small-displacement scaling fails, how far the fold lies from axial onset, and which of the emerging branches are centers or saddles. These are usable reference data for studying this concrete flow. The correction to the independence claim preserves this result and explicitly locates where the two conserved quantities cease to give independent coordinates; the value is the model-specific diagram, not the generic fold or fourth-root exponent alone.
residual_risks: This is a local conservative benchmark, not evidence of chaotic dynamics or conclusions about other parameter regimes.
